summary.headline: Signpost India FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore with EBITDA margin up ~590 bps to 25.5%; management guides 20%+ growth and 25-27% margin for FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 46% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR162 crore, with operating EBITDA more than tripling YoY to INR42 crore at a 26.3% margin. FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR576 crore, EBITDA rose 65% to INR147 crore and net profit more than doubled to INR70 crore. Receivables rose about 80% YoY to INR317 crore, which management attributed to multi-city campaigns requiring regional compliance approvals, and it targets faster collections by Q3 FY27 through milestone-based billing. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 net profit / net margin

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled from 7.5% margin in FY25

segments.name: Transit media
segments.commentary: Management calls transit the primary focus on long-term contracts; industry transit segment grew 22% in 2025 to INR20.2 billion. Bangalore Metro stations under contract rose from 18 to 25 against 67 stations on the line.

segments.name: Digital out-of-home (DOOH)
segments.commentary: Management cites DOOH as a higher-margin contributor; digital ad space reportedly rose from 25,000 sq ft to 80,000 sq ft between Q3 and Q4. Transit and digital together are about 48% of FY26 top line.

segments.name: Street furniture / bus queue shelters
segments.commentary: Mumbai contract requires 20% of about 3,000 bus queue shelters to be upgraded within 3 years; about 11% completed so far. Digitisation is not a binding commitment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to be in double digits; management also cited 20%+ growth in one answer.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 25-27%, supported by operating leverage, better utilisation and rising DOOH mix.
FY27 capex of about INR60-75 crore across infrastructure, capacity and technology.
Targets 6-7% cost saving on cost of services without hurting top line; management said this would flow directly to PBT.
About 48% of FY26 revenue (INR576 crore) is already contracted for FY27 per management.
Working-capital cycle targeted to improve via milestone-based billing by Q3 FY27; industry norm 90-120 days.
Mid-term ambition of 100 cities nationwide from more than 30 currently; asset-light model with data layer planned.
capex_capacity: Footprint grew from 4 cities at 2024 listing to 32 cities; about 866,000 sq ft added in FY26.
FY27 capex planned at INR60-75 crore across infrastructure, capacity expansion and technology implementation.
Kolkata Streetscape Renaissance project expected to reach 60-70% implementation by Sept-Oct 2026, before Durga Puja.
Bangalore Metro expansion ramping: 18 to 25 stations now generating revenue against 67 stations on the line.
Electric premium bus fleet additions across Mumbai, Hyderabad and Goa.
Management says new assets typically take 4-6 months to mature; some (e.g., Shimla) take 5-6 months.
demand_pricing: Management says around 3/4 of revenue is direct from advertisers; anchor client share about 29% of revenue; over 1,600 active advertisers.
Management cites FICCI-EY data: organised OOH market grew 13% in 2025 to INR66.9 billion, projected about INR85 billion by 2028; DOOH about 18% share, transit about 30%.
Management says customer mix includes PSUs and fintech/banking (e.g., SBI, NPCI, PNB), with FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI as other key categories.
Management says it is shifting from short-term intermediary-led campaigns toward multi-month and annual brand contracts; average remaining contract tenure about 14 years.
Most contracts are minimum-guarantee (fixed licence fee) models; revenue-share contracts are below 10% of portfolio, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables increase (noted as higher this quarter) be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to multi-city campaigns where regional office approvals delay invoicing; milestone-based billing is being pushed with clients, targeting improvement by Q3 FY27. Bill discounting was explored but rejected due to added cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue cross INR1,000 crore by 2029?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 48% of FY26 revenue is already in the FY27 engine and it would be 'the first person to see that number in 2029', but it could not assure that target.

qa_highlights.question: What drives gross margin and how much can cost fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of services includes licence costs and production/display costs such as Wi-Fi and power; management sees a 7-8% scope to reduce these costs next year without hurting top line. Most licences are minimum-guarantee, not linked to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Sector split of revenue and receivable sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numbers; said PSU/government-linked and FMCG, education, MSME and BFSI are the main categories, not real estate or luxury brands.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin move to 30% in 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new geographies need 4-6 months to mature and gave no margin target beyond the 25-27% EBITDA range guidance; Bangalore Metro ramp was cited as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of recent contracts (Kolkata, Bengaluru Metro, OMC petrol pump hoardings)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata implementation expected at 60-70% by Sept-Oct 2026; Bangalore Metro stations now generating revenue, with some signed for 2-3 years; FY27 growth expected at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited multi-city techno-commercial bidding track record, 7+ year contract tenures, direct advertiser relationships and the Captura AI planning platform; example of MSRDC bid where 27 agencies bid and few qualified.

qa_highlights.question: Founder shareholding fell from 66% to 44% after merger with Pressman; rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on valuation; said Pressman promoters converted equity to non-promoter base due to family losses and age.

qa_highlights.question: How many Mumbai bus queue shelters are digitised?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract requires 20% of about 3,000 shelters to be upgraded (refurbishment, not necessarily digital) within 3 years; about 11% completed. Digital is at company's discretion.

risks_watch: Receivables up ~80% YoY to INR317 crore; cash conversion depends on milestone billing delivering by Q3 FY27.
Management has not disclosed the receivable ageing split (over vs under 6 months), which was asked directly.
Gross margin dependence on minimum-guarantee licence fees, which are fixed regardless of revenue.
New geographies and contracts (Kolkata, Bangalore Metro, bus fleets) require 4-6 months maturity; execution and ramp timing unproven.
Management's FY27 guidance is mixed (double-digit growth in one answer, 20%+ in another); clarity needed.
Founder/promoter holding dropped from 66% to 44% post-merger; management declined to comment on valuation rationale.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, asset-light strategy and the DOOH mix, but evasive on receivable ageing, sector revenue split, margin upside beyond guidance and the merger valuation. Management repeatedly deferred to Q3 FY27 for collections improvement.
key_quotes: So instead of selling the spaces, we are smartly building the spaces and trying to generate a better yield on the same spaces.

So the milestone -based billing we have pushed that whatever we get the compliance from whichever region or a city, that money will be clocked into the account and it will not be in our email box of a check.
I'm not saying it's a normal path, it is a unusual path what we have taken instead of depending on the intermediaries, we are taking the approach because we have a national presence.
